picks.headline: Three Last-Minute Packers vs. Vikings Predictions
picks.blurb: Three Last-Minute Packers vs. Vikings Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates Women's Top 25 NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers Men's Top 25 CFP projections Three Last-Minute Packers vs. Vikings Predictions (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 15, 2026 at 2:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are set to host the Minnesota Vikings in what is easily the biggest game of the season up to this point. After getting embarrassed in Week 1 by the Vikings, this is a revenge game for a Packers team that is 5-1 in their last six games. Minnesota recently traded for Kirk Cousins, so that's been one of the key talking points going into this one. Green Bay is a bit banged up , but so is every team at this point in the season. For the second time this year, the Vikings are able to avoid Micah Parsons, though Minnesota is out a pair of key players themselves. Cousins has thrown an interception in five of the nine games he's played this year. His season began with a two-interception game against the Miami Dolphins, and he's fresh off a three-interception contest in San Francisco. This Packers defense has been on an absolute tear, and even with Xavier McKinney being questionable, there are more than enough playmakers who can capitalize on the 38-year-old's return to the Vikings. There could be a few reasons for why this happens, but Green Bay needs a big game from Kaleb Johnson. Johnson looked great in Week 9 when Josh Jacobs broke his finger, and if there was ever a time to get the run game going, it's against this Vikings defense. Sure, Love is coming off a monstrous 372-yard performance, but Minnesota isn't about to let him throw for nearly 400 yards again. Love has thrown for 300+ yards four times this season. He's finished with at least 274 passing yards in each of his last five games. Obviously, Packers fans will try to go against this prediction as he threw for 387 yards in Week 1, but Minnesota's defense has only gotten better since that point. Lambeau Field is going to be in for a treat on Sunday, Nov. 15. The NFC North has proven it's the best division in all of football, and Matt LaFleur's squad is going to go all out with a bye next weekend. Trey Smack has had his fair share of struggles this season, but he's also been locked in throughout a few key moments. In all likelihood, this will be a close game that comes down to the wire, so every point matters, and there's a real chance the Packers could give Smack a chance to win the game.

away.headline: Vikings vs. Packers live player stats, box score and match stats for Kirk Cousins' return in NFL Week 10

away.blurb: Packers list seven questionable, rule out four vs. Vikings | Week 10 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News S Xavier McKinney (foot) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday Evan Siegle, packers.com S Xavier McKinney GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed seven players questionable and ruled out four for Sunday's NFC North showdown with the Minnesota Vikings at Lambeau Field. The seven questionable are safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) and running back Chris Brooks (ankle). Running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) have been ruled out. Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) has been listed as doubtful after not practicing this week. McKinney was added to the injury report Friday after being listed as limited in practice. He has not missed a game due to injury since 2022 with the New York Giants. Moore and Brooks are currently on injured reserve with a designation to return and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play Sunday. Moore got off to a fast start as Green Bay's primary kickoff and punt returner before injuring his ankle against Chicago last month. He's averaging 16.0 yards per punt return with a 27.5-yard average on kickoffs. Green Bay's starting nickel cornerback returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. He's played in 31 consecutive games for the Packers (including playoffs). Van Ness, who leads the Packers with 13 quarterback hits and 4½ sacks this season, played 32 snaps in Sunday's 45-27 win over New England but did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday before returning in a limited capacity. Kicker Trey Smack (right calf), linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper (illness), guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) didn't receive a game status and will be available Sunday. The Vikings have ruled out quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion), defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest). Outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy (calf), S Joshua Metellus (shoulder) and receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) are questionable. Minnesota didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: safety Jay Ward (knee), safety Theo Jackson (quad), tackle Christian Darrisaw (rest), safety Harrison Smith (rest) and quarterback Carson Wentz (ankle). ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window * The Vikings did not practice on Wednesday; the report is an estimation. news Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday CB Keisean Nixon has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's game

home.headline: Packers list 12 players with status designations on final Week 10 injury report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players with status designations on the final Week 10 injury report, including seven players listed as questionable to play on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings . Of the 12, three are designated to return from injury lists and are not part of the 53-man roster, so nine players -- or roughly 17 percent of the roster -- have status designations for Sunday. Edge rusher Micah Parsons, running back Josh Jacobs, center Sean Rhyan and tight end Josh Whyle were ruled out on Friday, while linebacker Zaire Franklin -- who has missed three straight games and didn't practice this week -- is doubtful to play. Parsons is still ramping up after returning to practice last week, Jacobs needs surgery on his broken finger, Rhyan will miss his third straight game with an ankle injury and Whyle is out for the second straight game due to a concussion. The seven players listed as questionable, with associated injuries: McKinney was a late add to the injury report on Friday with a foot injury. Brooks and Moore are designated to return from injured reserve but would need to be activated to the 53-man roster on Saturday to play Sunday. Van Ness and Bullard didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday with new injuries but returned in a limited capacity on Friday. Zeitler added a new injury (triceps) before Friday's practice and didn't participate. Inactives are released 90 minutes before kickoff, so we likely won't know more about the seven players listed as questionable to play until around 10:30 a.m. CT on Sunday morning. G Kevin Zeitler (ankle, triceps) Expect several roster moves on Saturday. The Packers need to activate Brooks and/or Moore to the 53 and elevate one or two players from the practice squad to the gameday roster for Week 10. Of course, that won't help them when the Jacksonville Jaguars come to town. Although, none of us expect Tennessee to take this one lying down. Here's the staff's latest round of Titans predictions. Lane: Titans 23, Jaguars 34 Echoing what my fellow writers will say, I believe the Titans put on a more than fair scoring performance in this one. I expect Cam Ward to continue to improve, even without Carnell Tate ; it's the defense, after trading both Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker, that is more likely to falter. At 6-2 in the hunt for a championship run, Jacksonville is simply leaps and bounds ahead of Tennessee. The two teams are a part of the same process, but the Jags' rebuild could be considered done and over with. The Titans' feels like it will never end. But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week. “I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week. "It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice." How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans. Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late. The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate. But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control. On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. picks.blurb: Prediction For Jaguars’ Week 10 Showdown with the Tennessee Titans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Latest NFL updates Women's Top 25 NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers Men's Top 25 CFP projections Prediction For Jaguars’ Week 10 Showdown with the Tennessee Titans (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jacksonville Jaguars enter their road matchup against the Tennessee Titans as 10.5-point favorites. The Jaguars are rolling at 6-2 and have been dominating their opponents all season. Jacksonville has four wins by at least 23 points this year. No other team in the league has more than one such victory. The Titans, on the other hand, are in last place in the AFC South with a 1-7 record and have (again) started to rebuild for the future. Gone are star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who is one of the best defensive players in the entire league, and safety Amani Hooker, who leads the NFL with five interceptions. Both were traded before the NFL's trade deadline this past Tuesday. Trading Simmons netted the Titans two first-round picks from the Chicago Bears , while trading Hooker (and a fifth-rounder) to the Buffalo Bills brought back a second-round pick. On paper, this game looks like a mismatch. Jacksonville is one of the NFL's elite teams, while Tennessee is one of the worst. In addition to Simmons and Hooker, the Titans will also be without five injured starters on Sunday, including top rookies WR Carnell Tate and LB Anthony Hill Jr. However, it is still a divisional matchup, which is always tough no matter each team's record. Not taking Tennessee lightly was the first of my five keys to a Jaguars victory. If Jacksonville remains as focused on the Titans as it was on the Colts and Ravens in the past two weeks, this one could get ugly quickly. If the Jaguars get caught looking ahead to next week's road tilt against the first-place New York Giants , Jacksonville could fall victim to a huge upset. Don't bet on that happening. Jacksonville's high-powered offense will be going against a Tennessee defense that ranks 31st in both total yards and passing yards allowed. The Titans give up about 382 yards per game, 258 of which come through the air. Their run defense gives up about 124 yards per game, which is still only 22nd in the NFL. Tennessee gives up 24.9 points per game, which ranks 23rd. Those numbers were all with Simmons and Hooker. Jacksonville's offense, meanwhile, is averaging about 346 yards per game, and its average of 28.6 points per contest is the fourth-most in the league. Trevor Lawrence and Co. should have a field day. Defensively, the Jaguars give up only 15.1 points per game, the second-fewest in the league. Their run defense ranks fifth at about 89 yards per game. That is after the Jaguars gave up 172 rushing yards against Baltimore last week, many of which came during garbage time of Jacksonville's 33–10 win. The Jaguars should be able to dominate for the third week in a row. Unless Jacksonville gets caught looking past the Titans, the team should easily improve to 7-2 and continue flexing its muscles as one of the NFL's top Super Bowl contenders. Given the results of Jacksonville's last two games against inferior opponents, I don't expect the Jaguars to fall victim to a trap game. Prediction: Jaguars 38, Titans 9

The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have lost their top two cornerbacks to injury in the second half of Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins . The injury history of both Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward makes both reports concerning. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Ward suffered three concussions in his first season in Indianapolis after signing a three-year deal worth up to $54 million to be the team’s No. 1 cornerback. Ward missed time due to a back injury in training camp, a groin injury suffered against Kansas City and now the shin injury. Gardner’s injury was, again, to his calf; he's dealt with ongoing issues to that part of his leg. When he returned for the 2026 season, Gardner was optimistic that he’d put the calf issues behind him. But Gardner suffered another calf injury in the team’s loss to the Titans and missed a game. Gardner was optimistic at the time because the point of the strain was in a different part of his calf muscle, but he missed a game due to the injury. It is unclear if the calf injury Gardner suffered against Miami on Sunday is the same leg, but if it is, there are significant concerns moving forward for a player who is under contract in Indianapolis long-term. While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season. On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns). The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key. Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility. However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude. Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease. away.headline: Struggling Panthers could get 5 starters, 4 reserves back from injuries in the coming weeks
away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress. The Panthers are also hopeful to get left tackle Ickey Ekwonu and cornerback Jaycee Horn back in the coming weeks. That’s five starters — Jackson, Phillips, Lewis, Ekwonu and Horn — and four key reserves potentially returning for the stretch run. The Panthers (3-5) needed some good news. They've lost three straight, although they remain tied with New Orleans for first place in the NFC South. Tampa Bay and Atlanta, both 3-6, are lurking right behind in a division that any team can win if it can just, well, win. “The guys who can help us right now, we will have them up,” Canales said. One of the reasons the Panthers were so quiet at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday is that they have so many players returning from injuries, Canales said. “I'm excited about the guys that we have that are staring right at us and are going to come back to us in whatever order that may look like,” Canales said. “We feel really strong about this group and I have a lot of confidence in the guys that we have in this locker room.” Jackson, in particular, could provide a boost this week. Carolina's secondary has been hit hard with Jackson and Horn missing the last five games. With Lee and Akayleb Evans also hurt, Carolina was down to starting its fifth and sixth cornerbacks — Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton — on Sunday against the Denver Broncos. away.blurb: Carolina Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley has received an NFL fine for the controversial hit that knocked Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle out of their Week 9 matchup with a concussion. The play occurred with 19 seconds remaining in the first quarter of Carolina's 26-21 loss to Denver on November 8. Wheatley was not penalized for the hit during the game, despite Waddle subsequently entering concussion protocol and being ruled out. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. home.blurb: Etienne had been out of action since suffering a hamstring injury during a Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. The Panthers represent a soft landing spot for Etienne should he indeed return to the lineup on Sunday, as they rank 28th in the NFL against the run this season. New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s five-game absence reportedly may come to an end Sunday. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the Saints plan to activate Etienne from injured reserve, putting him in line to play against the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon. ▶️ Full Raiders-Saints Recap 05:42 After racking up 1,399 total yards from scrimmage and 13 touchdowns with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, Etienne cashed in by signing a four-year, $47.4 million contract with the Saints in free agency. Sharing the backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller, Etienne was off to a relatively slow start through his first three games with New Orleans, rushing for 128 yards and no touchdowns on 30 carries, while also catching 11 passes for 51 yards. While Etienne was not being used as an every-down back, his efficiency was solid, averaging 4.3 yards per carry, which matched the second-best average of his career from last season. The 27-year-old Etienne is now set to rejoin what remains a crowded backfield with Kamara and Audric Estimé in the mix. Miller was released by New Orleans last week. It would be fair to expect head coach Kellen Moore to re-integrate Etienne slowly given the nature of the injury he is returning from and how much it can impact a running back. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. home.headline: Las Vegas Raiders just got the best news they could have asked for regarding Brock Bowers' injury
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: The Raiders couldn’t do anything in the passing game when Bowers was out. Heck, even when he was playing, they couldn't do much. The Seahawks have one of the best defenses in the league, if not the best. The Las Vegas Raiders ended up losing tight end Brock Bowers during their game to the Seattle Seahawks, as he left with an ankle injury The Las Vegas Raiders just got about as good news as they could get about Brock Bowers' injury sustained against the Seattle Seahawks . According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Media , Brock Bowers is believed to have avoided a big ankle injury. Per Rapoport, he is more day-to-day than week-to-week. The Raiders will run more tests on the ankle. He was injured early in the first quarter. He rolled his ankle after he was blocked on a run play . Then he went to the tent and may have even gone back to the locker room. He did that a few times because he came back in that game. He actually caught another ball after being injured. But something happened again, and while we didn't quite see it, maybe Bowers decided he couldn't keep going. Or maybe the staff decided they had to pull him for his future. Bowers finished the game with two catches for 18 yards, second on the team in receiving at the time he left. Raiders are going to need someone to step up if Brock Bowers can't go And they made sure the Raiders would have a tough time doing anything. Then some fans complained that Klint Kubiak kept running the ball late in the game when it wasn't working. Well, he did that to avoid his QB from getting hit even more. Raiders receivers also didn’t separate well in this game. Mendoza delivered some really nice balls to receivers. They were either covered too well, dropped it, or fell in their route. Someone has to step up and help Mendoza. Next week could be easier, but only because Vegas' defense will have to face the offense. The Broncos aren't a great offensive team, but that defense may be just as good as Seattle's. The Las Vegas Raiders have a A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Mon, Nov 16). McVay said Monday that the Rams expect Nacua to land on injured reserve, although he did not provide a specific timetable for his return. On Sunday, roughly two-thirds of Stafford’s passing yards went to one player. The Rams should have more ways to move the chains on third-and-11 than waiting for Nacua to get open again, especially if he is not going to be available for the immediate future. Puka Nacua had already caught 14 passes, piled up 150 receiving yards, and scored the go-ahead touchdown when the Los Angeles Rams gave him the ball one more time. He gained five yards on the ground and hurt his right knee on Los Angeles’ final offensive snap. The Rams left Washington with a 20-13 win and another major injury problem at wide receiver. Dan Orlovsky, Matthew Stafford’s former backup in Detroit, would have been shopping for a receiver before that handoff. With Davante Adams already on injured reserve and the trade deadline a day away, the ESPN analyst wants the Rams to make a move. There’s four or five clips where I’m like, he’s just not seeing it,” Orlovsky added. “It is very Puka-centric, and they’re slow starting on offense right now. away.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
home.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. Plus, how to watch, what to know, and a prediction Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati. Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign. home.blurb: However, you don’t dismantle a division rival who entered the game off a bye with a top-10 defense so thoroughly with one dynamic player. Yes, Burrow was sensational again, but the real standout was an offensive line that completely snuffed out the Steelers' pass rush. It was a defense that stood up and shut down everything Aaron Rodgers tried. Playmakers made plays, and the Bengals dominated in the trenches. For years, the Bengals have had an array of weapons at Burrow’s disposal: Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins , Chase Brown . They’re not new. What’s different about this iteration is the offensive line. The unit was were overpowering on Sunday night. Pittsburgh entered the evening ranking sixth in sacks. They barely sniffed Burrow, earning one sack and just 10 QB pressures. Yes, Burrow got the ball out quick, but it wasn’t simply the QB knowing where the rushers were coming from. The O-line worked seamlessly to stymie the Steelers. Right tackle Amarius Mims was uber impressive, allowing one pressure on 44 snaps. Against star T.J. Watt , he allowed zero pressures on 23 snaps, including 22 one-on-one reps, per Next Gen Stats. Dominant. The Steelers, with a cushy schedule and veteran talent, aren’t out of the race yet. But Pittsburgh has some soul-searching to do after the Bengals snatched it on Sunday night. It was easy to suggest that Kirk Cousins ' return to Minnesota would jumpstart an offense that made a limp noodle look rigid through the first eight games. On paper, the match was ideal. Far too often in the NFL, however, the paper tells lies. His first big third-down throw showed the difference between Cousins and the rest of the QBs the Vikings have trotted out the past two seasons. Facing a third-and-23 in the first quarter, Kirko didn't dump it off for a 4-yard gain and yet another field goal (yawn). Nope. He launched that pigskin up the seam to Myles Price , who snagged it and took it to paydirt. Cousins was excellent on third downs, going 9 of 12 for 110 yards, a TD, an INT and one sack. "How are you able to respond when things go bad? Obviously we didn't respond well today, and that starts with me. ... But having the opportunity to play, that's what allows us to stay focused. To be out there is fun. Football is fun." He might not have the consistency of a regular starter for a winning team, but McCord could carve out a solid career as a spot-starting backup. home.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . home.blurb: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals Skip to main content SI.COM According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warm-ups at Paycor Stadium and has been ruled out vs. Cincinnati as a result. Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati. Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign. Holding up in coverage as a group on the back end of the defense against the likes of Chase and Higgins would've been a big ask even with Elliott on the field, though, and being down a veteran like that could have reverberating effects when facing a passing offense that averages the most yards per game (285.5) in the league. away.blurb: Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 The Chargers began their prep for the Ravens with a whopping 18 players listed on their Thursday injury report. Of those players, over half of them sat out with a DNP tag. That group of nine included wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), offensive guard/tackle Branson Taylor (ankle), defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe (ankle), and cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle). Every other player was given a limited designation. That group includes tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman, both of whom are likely to be activated this week off of IR. Offensive guard/tackle Trey Pipkins also had his practice window activated this week, although he did miss Thursday's practice altogether for personal reasons. Following the botched trade to the Broncos, linebacker Daiyan Henley was a DNP Thursday for personal reasons. Jim Harbaugh told reporters prior to practice that Henley got back to LA from Denver late Wednesday night and his attendance on Thursday was always going to be TBD. McConkey's injury continuing to keep him out of practice is worrisome. After being completely off the final injury report before the Texans game, he never made it onto the field as sudden back spasms kept him from playing. Now, four days later, those back spasms are still enough of a problem to keep him from practicing. This is most certainly something to monitor this week. away.headline: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report
away.blurb: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report Skip to main content SI.COM The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, they just had a final hour trade before the trade deadline fall through and they are still searching for any sort of identity on offense. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? thursday's injury report for week 10 at BAL pic.twitter.com/fXSvi1MmEt It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit. Published Nov 14, 2026 THOMAS MARTINEZ Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs.

home.headline: Ravens’ Jesse Minter addresses statement on Lamar Jackson: ‘Same page’

Randall is listed as questionable, while Hawkins was ruled out. Jackson underwent surgery to repair the broken and dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand, Minter said Friday in a statement after declining to discuss the matter earlier in the week. Asked on Saturday what prompted him to make a statement, he said he wanted to “get it out there” so that there was “less speculation” about the injury and a timeline for a possible return. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey, who has dealt with a slew of injuries, including a back injury that kept him out of last week’s game against the Houston Texans, was listed as questionable after being limited in practice Saturday. It was his first practice of the week. Also questionable are starting left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), starting defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), rotational linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), tight end David Njoku (fibula) and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III (knee). Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful, while cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), safety Kendall Williamson (calf) and offensive lineman Branson Taylor (ankle) are all out. A few extra days off proved beneficial to the Ravens. Hawkins, who signed a two-year, $10 million free agent deal with Baltimore this offseason but has largely struggled even when healthy, hasn’t played since a Week 6 loss to the Browns in Cleveland. Baltimore has until 4 p.m. Saturday to activate Randall for this week’s game and until Wednesday to activate him or he would revert to season-ending injured reserve. home.headline: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.
